<description>
Several numeric options were read with GetArg<int>() and then stored into unsigned or wider members without a range check. A negative value wrapped to a huge value and disabled the limit it was meant to configure, and a value wider than the destination could silently become a different number.

Parse the options whose destination is unsigned with ToIntegral<T>() on the raw string rather than with GetArg<T>(): the typed getter saturates values it cannot represent (so a leading '-' for an unsigned T becomes 0), while ToIntegral rejects '-', trailing garbage and overflow instead of saturating. Reject the remaining out-of-range values where they are read:

- -maxtipage: uint32_t seconds, range [0, UINT32_MAX]. A negative age placed the IBD cutoff in the future, so the node never treated its tip as recent.
- -dbbatchsize: uint64_t bytes. A negative value wrapped to a huge batch size and disabled flushing, so a reindex could hold an unbounded batch.
- -dbcrashratio: uint32_t, range [0, UINT32_MAX]. CoinsViewOptions::simulate_crash_ratio is changed from int to uint32_t to match.
- -limitclustercount: [1, MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT_LIMIT]. The separate upper-bound check in ApplyArgsManOptions is folded into this one, so an invalid value is reported once with one message.
- -limitclustersize: [1, INT64_MAX / 1000] kB. Zero made every transaction exceed the cluster size and blocked all mempool admission.
- -limitancestorcount, -limitdescendantcount: non-negative.
- -mempoolexpiry: [0, std::chrono::seconds::max() / 3600] hours, and the value is stored as seconds directly. The bound is taken from seconds rather than hours because std::chrono::hours is not guaranteed to be 64-bit.
- -datacarriersize: [0, UINT_MAX]; still unchecked when -datacarrier=0 turns the limit off.
- -bytespersigop: [0, UINT_MAX]. A negative value wrapped and inflated the sigop-adjusted size of every transaction until all were non-standard.
- -maxsendbuffer, -maxreceivebuffer: [0, UINT_MAX / 1000], since both are multiplied by 1000 into unsigned int members.
- -bantime: greater than 0. Zero or negative made setban without an explicit duration create an already expired ban.
- -timeout: positive and at most INT_MAX milliseconds. A non-positive value now fails instead of silently falling back to the default (as -peertimeout already did), and a value above INT_MAX used to narrow before it could be checked (e.g. 2^32 + 1 became 1).
- -txconfirmtarget: [1, UINT_MAX] in parameter interaction, and additionally bounded by the fee estimator's maximum when a wallet is loaded. A target beyond the estimator's range made every transaction fall back to -fallbackfee. The help text now states the minimum.

Zero remains valid wherever it already meant "disabled": -dbbatchsize, -datacarriersize, -mempoolexpiry, -maxtipage, -bytespersigop, -maxsendbuffer, -maxreceivebuffer, -limitancestorcount and -limitdescendantcount.

Since -nofoo is parsed as 0, add DISALLOW_NEGATION to the options where 0 is valid but very different from "no limit": -dbbatchsize, -mempoolexpiry, -maxreceivebuffer, -maxsendbuffer, -maxtipage, -limitancestorcount, -limitdescendantcount and -datacarriersize. Options that already reject (-bantime, -timeout, -peertimeout, -limitclustercount, -limitclustersize, -txconfirmtarget) need no separate check: negation reports the value error once. -bytespersigop still allows negation, because 0 turns the sigop adjustment off, which is exactly what -nobytespersigop says.

ReadCoinsViewArgs now returns util::Result<void> (marked [[nodiscard]]) so its errors abort startup instead of being discarded.

Finally, -help gains the =<n> placeholder for the options that take a value (-dbbatchsize, -bytespersigop, -datacarriersize, -stopatheight, -checkblockindex) and states the bounds for -bantime, -limitclustercount, -limitclustersize and -txconfirmtarget.

Add unit tests for the option parsers and functional tests for the accepted, rejected and negated forms.
</description>

diff --git a/src/node/coins_view_args.cpp b/src/node/coins_view_args.cpp
index b781ea6b75..79845bf6cf 100644
--- a/src/node/coins_view_args.cpp
+++ b/src/node/coins_view_args.cpp
@@ -5,12 +5,40 @@
 #include <node/coins_view_args.h>
 
 #include <common/args.h>
+#include <tinyformat.h>
 #include <txdb.h>
+#include <util/result.h>
+#include <util/strencodings.h>
+#include <util/translation.h>
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <limits>
 
 namespace node {
-void ReadCoinsViewArgs(const ArgsManager& args, CoinsViewOptions& options)
+util::Result<void> ReadCoinsViewArgs(const ArgsManager& args, CoinsViewOptions& options)
 {
-    if (auto value = args.GetIntArg("-dbbatchsize")) options.batch_write_bytes = *value;
-    if (auto value = args.GetIntArg("-dbcrashratio")) options.simulate_crash_ratio = *value;
+    if (const auto arg{args.GetArg("-dbbatchsize")}) {
+        // Parse into the destination's width. A negative value would wrap to a huge
+        // batch size and disable flushing entirely, so it must be rejected; ToIntegral
+        // is used rather than GetArg<uint64_t>() because the typed getter saturates
+        // values that fail to parse, so "-dbbatchsize=-1" would silently become 0.
+        const auto bytes{ToIntegral<uint64_t>(*arg)};
+        if (!bytes) {
+            return util::Error{Untranslated(strprintf("-dbbatchsize must be a non-negative number of bytes (got %s).", *arg))};
+        }
+        options.batch_write_bytes = *bytes;
+    }
+    if (const auto arg{args.GetArg("-dbcrashratio")}) {
+        // simulate_crash_ratio is uint32_t, so parse straight into that width. A
+        // negative value would otherwise become a huge ratio (or trip the positivity
+        // assumption inside FastRandomContext::randrange), and a value above the
+        // destination's range would narrow to a different ratio than requested.
+        const auto ratio{ToIntegral<uint32_t>(*arg)};
+        if (!ratio) {
+            return util::Error{Untranslated(strprintf("-dbcrashratio must be between 0 and %u (got %s).", std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max(), *arg))};
+        }
+        options.simulate_crash_ratio = *ratio;
+    }
+    return {};
 }
 } // namespace node

+Updated settings
+----------------
+
+- Several numeric options now reject values outside the range they are stored
+  in, instead of silently wrapping to a huge value, inverting, or falling back
+  to the default. Configurations that start on previous releases can therefore
+  fail to start after upgrading; check for these options in `bitcoin.conf` and
+  the command line if a node reports one of the new errors. Examples that used
+  to be accepted are `-timeout=0`, `-bantime=0`, `-limitclustersize=0`,
+  `-limitclustercount=0`, and `-txconfirmtarget=0`, or above 1008 when a wallet
+  is loaded.
+
+  - Options that now require a value greater than zero:
+
+    - `-bantime`: zero or negative previously produced bans that had already
+      expired.
+    - `-timeout`: zero or negative previously fell back to the default
+      silently. The value is in milliseconds and must not exceed 2147483647.
+    - `-limitclustersize`: zero made every transaction exceed the cluster size
+      limit. Negative values wrapped to an effectively unlimited limit. The
+      maximum is 9223372036854775 kilobytes.
+    - `-limitclustercount`: the accepted range is 1 to 64.
+    - `-txconfirmtarget`: the accepted range is 1 to 4294967295, and it is also
+      capped at the highest confirmation target the fee estimator tracks (1008
+      by default) when a wallet is loaded. Previously a target above that range
+      made every transaction fall back to `-fallbackfee`. `-blocksonly` starts
+      no fee estimator, so the estimator cap does not apply in that mode.
+
+  - Options that still accept zero, which keeps its existing meaning of
+    "disabled" or "unlimited", but now reject negative and oversized values:
+
+    - `-maxtipage`: at most 4294967295 seconds. A negative value placed the
+      initial block download cutoff in the future, so the node never treated
+      its tip as recent.
+    - `-mempoolexpiry`: at most 2562047788015215 hours. A negative value
+      expired ordinary transactions instead of keeping them.
+    - `-dbbatchsize` and `-dbcrashratio`: `-dbbatchsize` is at most
+      18446744073709551615 bytes and `-dbcrashratio` at most 4294967295. A
+      negative `-dbbatchsize` disabled batch flushing.
+    - `-datacarriersize` and `-bytespersigop`: at most 4294967295. Negative
+      values previously wrapped and, for `-bytespersigop`, made every
+      transaction non-standard.
+    - `-maxsendbuffer` and `-maxreceivebuffer`: at most 4294967, since the
+      value is multiplied by 1000 to give bytes.
+    - `-limitancestorcount` and `-limitdescendantcount`.
+
+- Negating a setting (`-nofoo`) has always been read as setting it to zero.
+  For `-dbbatchsize`, `-mempoolexpiry`, `-maxreceivebuffer`, `-maxsendbuffer`,
+  `-maxtipage`, `-limitancestorcount`, `-limitdescendantcount` and
+  `-datacarriersize`, zero is valid but means something very different from
+  "no limit", so `-nofoo` is now rejected instead of quietly turning the limit
+  off. The options that already reject zero report the same error for `-nofoo`
+  as for `-foo=0`. `-bytespersigop` still accepts `-nobytespersigop`, because
+  zero turns the sigop adjustment off, which is what the negation says.
+
+- `-maxtipage`, `-dbbatchsize`, `-dbcrashratio` and `-limitclustercount` are
+  now parsed strictly, so a value with trailing characters such as
+  `-maxtipage=1h` is rejected instead of being truncated to the leading number.
+
+These changes were implemented via PR (#36861)
